linkedin_post:
Character.AI filed for bankruptcy on 12 October. In 2024 Google paid $2.7 billion for a licence to its technology and to hire its founders. Disney is now offering jobs to 66 of its staff at about $60 million a year, with a $20 million opening bid for the code, and the lawsuits stay behind.

So the money followed the people, and everyone else got the empty box.

If your business runs on someone else's AI, the full piece has four questions to ask your supplier: are its founders still there, is this its main product, is it short of cash, and is it piling up lawsuits.

Disney has asked a dying AI company to go bust, so it can hire the team and leave the lawsuits behind. Google paid $2.7 billion for the same company's founders two years ago. I read the court papers on Character.AI to work out why both giants paid for a piece of it, who is left holding the empty box, and what it means if your business runs on someone else's AI.
